reviewMode: fresh independent cross-review against candidate-free evidence

confidence.limits: Proposal content was visible before the full-cell semantic audit, so target selection has anchoring risk and is not a second blind review. Forty-two of forty-four proposed change targets match a primary or blind proposal; two are cross-derived. Confidence remains moderate for broad source meaning and clear terminology/grammar issues, and lower for idiomatic Hindi, Arabic, Vietnamese, and Indonesian. No native-speaker signoff was obtained.

processExposure.statement: The cross-review read only the three specified sealed packet directories. Before proposal content, I checked packet schemas/readmes/verifier code and all checksum inventories; I had made no row-level semantic decisions or target selections. The full blind review.json was opened before cell-by-cell semantic review. Primary proposal rows were opened after inspecting source IDs/text and caller-reference snippets, but before reviewing the full current-value matrix and before forming decisions. Proposal visibility influenced target selection: 42 of 44 recommended change targets exactly match a primary or blind proposal, while two are cross-derived. I then adjudicated all 240 cells against candidate-free source/current/caller evidence and recorded disagreements. This is a fresh cross-review, not a second blind review. It did not access a repository/worktree, PR body, prior window review decisions, external sources/search, or a browser. Checksum verification read packet files as bytes, including opaque prior-evidence reattestation files; those prior-window contents were not parsed or used as review decisions.
